name: Reflected cross-site scripting
mental_model: Untrusted request data is returned into a browser context that interprets data as executable content.
security_property: Request-controlled data must remain data in every output context unless explicitly trusted by design.
root_causes: Unsafe interpolation into executable browser contexts
signals: A unique inert marker is reflected
The reflection reaches an HTML, attribute, URL, style, or script context
The response applies no context-appropriate encoding

hypothesis_templates.statement: When {actor} supplies {marker} through {input}, {application} may place it into {sink} without context-appropriate encoding, causing controlled executable interpretation.
preconditions: The tested input and output surface are explicitly in scope
The marker is inert and researcher-controlled
hypothesis_templates.expected_safe_behaviour: The marker is encoded or placed in a non-executable context.
hypothesis_templates.expected_vulnerable_behaviour: The marker crosses into an executable output context without the required encoding.
hypothesis_templates.falsifier: The marker is absent, safely encoded, or cannot reach an executable context under the same controlled conditions.
stop_conditions: The test would require a harmful or persistent effect
Scope or browser-impact rules are ambiguous

safe_test_pattern: Use a unique inert marker, record the exact reflection context, compare encoded and unencoded local controls, and stop before any data or session access.
positive_controls: A trusted local value renders in the intended location
negative_controls: The same untrusted marker remains inert after context-appropriate encoding
falsifiers: The reflection is text-only in the exercised context
A browser parser cannot interpret the marker as executable content

minimum_evidence.description: Exact controlled input and resulting output-context observation.
Why the supplied data was untrusted and should remain non-executable.
A context-encoded negative control plus intended-render positive control.
A clean-session repeat using only the controlled marker.
Human statement limited to the demonstrated browser context and controlled effect.

common_false_positives: Encoding that looks unusual but remains parser-safe
A content-security control assumed to replace output encoding
impact_boundaries: Reflection alone does not prove script execution
Controlled execution does not prove session theft or account takeover
minimum_impact_rules: Use an inert marker or benign local signal
Do not read tokens, personal data, or third-party content
remediation: Apply context-appropriate output encoding at the sink
Prefer safe templating and text APIs
Use content security policy only as defence in depth
programme_policy_considerations: Respect rules for browser execution and social interaction
Preserve only the minimum response evidence

revisions.summary: Initial bounded reflected-output card and synthetic control fixture.
